items.author: Claude (sprint 33 batch completeness critic)
items.title: CREEDS claims every coined proper noun; three generation docs hold the machinery
items.design:
THE FINDING (2026-09-07, the sprint 33 batch critic). CREEDS.md's header makes the broadest ownership claim in the corpus - "how a cradle culture rolls its own phonology, and how every proper noun it coins is drawn from it". The machinery is documented elsewhere: NATION_GENERATION.md:275-325 (§ Pass 5 - Naming) holds world/tongue.{hpp,cpp}, culture::speech, coin_lexicon and its pure-function-of-the-tongue property, plus region names (:307) and city names (:320); PLANETOLOGY.md:764 asserts a third consumer, body names from tongue.hpp.

WHY IT SURVIVED EVERY SWEEP, and this is the part worth keeping: it is a ONE-WAY edge. CREEDS names NATION_GENERATION in its header; NATION_GENERATION does not name CREEDS. A boundary check scoped off MUTUAL "Confused with" pairs cannot see it, and the critic counted 89 one-way edges of which this is the clearest live overlap. Any tooling built for this class of defect (see BL-801, the header graph checker) must walk one-way edges, not just pairs.

THE WORK: decide whether CREEDS owns the tongue and the generation docs consume it, or CREEDS owns only the pantheon and the tongue belongs to generation. Then make the header match. Real history is never a name source - that rule is not at issue here, only the address of the machinery that enforces it.

items.author: Claude (sprint 33 batch completeness critic)
items.title: The ledgers README lists six Q&A docs; eight are on disk, and it contradicts itself forty lines later
items.design:
THE FINDING (2026-09-07, the sprint 33 batch critic; the header made it visible but the defect predates it). docs/ui/ledgers/README.md:9 claims it settles "which surfaces have a Q&A of their own". Its § The docs table lists SIX. `ls docs/ui/ledgers/` shows EIGHT: acquisitions, balance, construction, convoys, corporation, market, selection, tile_ledger. convoys.md and acquisitions.md are missing from the table - and the README's own § Cross-doc findings, about forty lines below the table, says of convoys "it... now has its own doc". The header, the table and the prose disagree inside one file.

THE WORK: reconcile the table against the directory. Small. Worth doing next to BL-801 (header graph checker), because a hand-maintained index of files that exist on disk is the thing a check should own.

items.author: Claude (sprint 33 batch completeness critic)
items.title: A check over the doc headers: dangling citations, one-way edges, and pairs that both claim a subject
items.design:
THE FINDING (2026-09-07). The sprint 33 batch scoped its three boundary lanes off defects a header-writing sweep HAPPENED to notice. That is not a search. The batch critic then built the Confused-with graph properly and immediately found a confirmed duplicate (BL-797, travel time doubled), a triple-assertion (BL-798, rung docs triple assert) and a one-way sprawl (BL-799, naming machinery sprawl) - none of which any lane would have reached.

TOOL CREATION IS SKILL CREATION, and the critic's throwaway script is exactly the tool this class of defect needs standing. It measured: 72 docs carry a header, 59 MUTUAL pairs, 89 ONE-WAY edges. A sweep scoped off mutual pairs alone is blind to the 89 - which is how BL-799 survived.

THE CHECK, as tools/session/header_graph.js:
  (a) DANGLING CITATIONS - every "DOC.md § Heading" reference in docs/ resolved against the target's actual headings. Two were found by hand in this batch (TOOLTIP citing a moved CANVASES section; SOLAR citing "LENSES.md § rung table", which does not exist). This half is objective and should FAIL, not warn.
  (b) THE HEADER GRAPH - mutual pairs and one-way edges from the Confused with / Not here lines, printed so a boundary sweep can be scoped off the whole graph rather than off what somebody noticed.
  (c) COVERAGE - every doc in CLAUDE.md § 3 carries a header; every doc carrying a header is in § 3. The orphan half is the router's staleness detector, exactly as ui_coverage.js orphans are the surface catalogue's.
  (d) STATE-INDEPENDENCE - a header carrying "landed", "built", "pending", "shipped" or a BL- id as status is a fail.

Do NOT try to detect a doubled SUBJECT automatically - that is judgement. The tool's job is to hand a human the candidate list and to fail hard on the objective half.

WRAP IT IN A SKILL once it runs (needs Ben's permission per CLAUDE.md § Tool creation is skill creation).

MORE FUEL FOR THE DANGLING-CITATION HALF (2026-09-07, found by the fix round's second cold reviewers, all confirmed independently). Beyond the two the batch repaired by hand, live references still name CONTRACTS headings the doc does not hold, in FOUR files across three kinds of artefact: src/world/corp_command.hpp, scripts/economy.lua, tools/verify/README.md and .claude/skills/verifier-headless/SKILL.md. And src/world/province.hpp:82 names "PROVINCES.md § The partition", a PREFIX of the real heading rather than the heading - resolvable by a human and by grep, invisible to an exact-match check.

TWO CONSEQUENCES FOR THE TOOL'S SCOPE, both learned the expensive way here: (a) it must sweep src/, scripts/, tools/ and .claude/ as well as docs/ - a citation in a header comment rots exactly like one in prose, and three of the six live misses were outside docs/; (b) it must flag PREFIX matches separately from exact misses, or the province.hpp class passes silently. A boundary move is precisely when these break, and hand-grepping for them is what the first UI lane claimed to have done and had not.

items.author: Claude (sprint 33 fix round, second cold reviews)
items.title: corp_command.hpp says two dormant verbs "still apply"; the implementation rejects them
items.design:
THE FINDING (2026-09-07, found by the economy lane's second cold reviewer while checking a pointer, confirmed independently). src/world/corp_command.hpp:96 says of accept_offer and abandon_contract that "They remain callable, and they still apply, ONLY because the enum is APPEND-ONLY". The implementation rejects them.

WHY IT IS WORTH A ROW RATHER THAN A SILENT EDIT: that comment is the HOME of the append-only invariant - the reason the two verbs may never be deleted is written there and nowhere else. A reader who tests the claim and finds it false has reason to distrust the invariant beside it, and the invariant is real: removing a verb renumbers every verb below it and breaks ACTIONS.json and every recorded command.

THE WORK: correct "they still apply" to what is true - they remain CALLABLE and are REJECTED, a dormant record and not a live mechanism - without weakening the append-only rule stated next to it. One comment. Also fix CONTRACTS.md:68, which names world.hpp for the three procurement verbs; the enum is in corp_command.hpp:30 and world.hpp holds no corp_verb.

items.author: Claude (sprint 33 fix round, second cold reviews)
items.title: FINANCE says material maintenance is a fixed 30%; the code reads an authored parameter
items.design:
THE FINDING (2026-09-07, raised by the economy lane's first cold reviewer and confirmed independently by its second). FINANCE.md:140-141 says "Material maintenance - a fixed 30 % floor of the building's maintenance constant". src/world/budget_system.cpp:41-46 says "Material cost: the authored idle floor (BL-739 - was a hard-coded 30%)" and computes `e.maintenance * idle_floor`. The 30% is gone from the code and survives in the doc.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE NOW THAN IT DID: pre-existing, but BL-794 (economy doc boundaries) routes both PRODUCTION and POPULATION readers to this section for the cost half of the workforce question. A stale figure two lines from where two docs now send everyone costs more than it did sitting alone.

THE WORK: state the floor as the authored parameter it is, naming BL-739 as the owner of the change rather than the number. One or two lines.

items.author: Claude (sprint 33 fix round, second cold reviews)
items.title: Two province-partition assertions are red, and the doc quotes a distribution the instrument no longer produces
items.design:
TWO FINDINGS, both from the generation lane's second cold reviewer (2026-09-07), both pre-existing and neither caused by the boundary move - but both now sit under PROVINCES, which the move made the sole owner.

(1) THE HARNESS IS RED. Two assertions in tools/verify/province_partition_harness.cpp fail in this tree. The reviewer flagged them precisely because it was asked to confirm P2b is GREEN, found that it is, and would not let a green single assertion imply a green harness. A broken check is worse than a failing one, and a partly-red harness that nobody reports reads as absent.

(2) THE MEASURED TABLE IS STALE. The distribution table the lane moved into PROVINCES no longer matches the instrument it names, and the pre-existing prose that reads the table is stale with it. It was carried across faithfully - the move is not the defect; the number is.

THE WORK: run the harness, establish whether the two red assertions are the code drifting or the check rotting, fix whichever is wrong, then re-measure the distribution and update the table and the prose that reads it together. Do not update the table from the failing harness without settling (1) first.

items.author: Claude (sprint 33 fix round, second cold reviews)
items.title: archiveFiles() has no callers, and --status cancelled no longer finds the 2026-08 purge
items.design:
TWO LOOSE ENDS LEFT BY BL-792 (the cold union), both raised by its second cold reviewer (2026-09-07) as notes rather than blockers.

(1) DEAD EXPORT. archiveFiles() now has zero callers anywhere in tools/ - archive_landed.js's two call sites moved to designFiles() - yet it stays exported under a comment that reads like a live contract. Either delete it or say in the comment that it is kept for external callers.

(2) A ROUTER PROMISE IS NOW HALF TRUE. CLAUDE.md says of the archive that "--status cancelled finds work that was closed unbuilt". The 186-row 2026-08-23 purge now reads status `purged`, not `cancelled`, so that search returns the 36 genuinely-cancelled rows and not the purge. The new state is more honest - a purge and a cancellation are different acts - but the router still describes the old one. Either widen the sentence to name both, or give the query a way to ask for closed-unbuilt across both.

Also worth one line while in there: the SWEEP_RE comment says the old allow-list "cost the union 620 rows"; measured it is 609 net, 625 raw.

items.author: Claude (header-coverage audit)
items.title: A stale twin of the style sheet sits in docs/development/design/, saying nothing is settled
items.design:
THE FINDING (2026-09-07, the header-coverage audit at the end of the sprint 33 batch - a doc with no header is how it surfaced).

docs/development/design/GLOBAL_STYLE_SHEET.md is 55 lines and opens "Status: **draft - iteration 0, nothing settled yet.**". The LIVE doc is docs/ui/design/GLOBAL_STYLE_SHEET.md at 232 lines, which CLAUDE.md § 3 names, which carries the sprint 33 header, and which every inbound citation points at (ui/RENDERING.md twice, ui/ICONS.md, research/CANVAS_RENDERING.md twice).

NOTHING POINTS AT THE DEVELOPMENT COPY. Its last touch is the commit that STARTED the ST1 style sprint; the work then moved to docs/ui/design/ and the original was never removed. docs/development/design/README.md and docs/development/design/renders/README.md are the same abandonment.

WHY IT IS WORTH A ROW RATHER THAN A QUIET DELETE: the stale copy does not merely duplicate - it CONTRADICTS. It says nothing is settled, on a subject where things have since been settled and promoted. A reader or an agent that reaches it by filename (both files are called GLOBAL_STYLE_SHEET.md) gets a confident, dated-looking answer that is false. That is the same shape as BL-798 (rung docs triple assert), at file grain instead of section grain.

THE WORK, and the call is Ben's because it is a deletion: confirm nothing references docs/development/design/ (verified today: nothing does), then remove the directory - or, if the render history under it is worth keeping, leave the renders and delete only the prose, with a one-line pointer at the live doc. Do not simply header the stale copy; a header on a dead twin makes it look maintained.

CHECK BEFORE DELETING: docs/development/design/renders/ against docs/ui/design/renders/ - if the older iterations exist only in the development copy, they are the reason to keep the directory.
